### B2436066 — Houston-only flood rows listed on a Chambers County site (planner) but not on the finder at a Chambers point: each source is scoped to the area it actually serves `[Site Planner / layers · Map finder]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #floodplain  *(owner, 2026-10-21: on Grand Port / Concept A (Chambers County, City of Baytown ETJ, plan group smqfy2r7pdec) the planner's Flood & Drainage lists Channels & ROW, Watersheds & BFE, Drainage Easements (HCFCD / BKDD data), Storm Sewer (City of Houston Public Works) and Master Plan Floodplains — none of whose sources serve Chambers County or Baytown — while the map finder centred on Mont Belvieu (also Chambers) listed only FEMA Flood Zones + Streams, Canals & Ditches. Follow-up to B2391216 (×2). DEDUPE-FIRST: B1091 / B1091(×2/×3) (flood-row relevance by county) is the mechanism that failed open here — this item replaces its input with a location rule, it does not re-open them.)*
**THE REAL DIFFERENCE (measured, so it is not rediscovered).** The brief's inference was right in kind and incomplete. (1) The planner scopes the district rows by `floodCounty`, computed in `LayerPanel` as: the site IDENTIFY county if it names exactly ONE, else **`null` when it names more than one** (a Baytown site straddles Harris and Chambers), else `siteCounty` (`restored?.county`, null until the identify/heal lands). **A null county fails OPEN** — `floodRowRelevance` / `districtReaches` / `areaCounties` all return "relevant" for an unknown county — so every Houston source is listed. The finder reasons over `countyForView`, which returns a real county for ANY point (polygon, else bbox, else nearest centre) and is never null; so it hid them. Pinned in `test/layerServiceAreas.test.js` ("the planner's null county no longer lets the Houston rows through"). (2) `REGION_ZONES.houston` was a 65-mile circle round downtown Houston that contains Chambers, Galveston and Brazoria, and its comment claimed HCFCD / BKDD / City of Houston data reach them — false. The circle is what the nine Houston-area rows used as their location rule, so it could not have saved a null-county planner. **Not reproduced on a throwaway:** a fresh located plan at Grand Port on the OLD production build (c574b64) healed its county to Chambers and listed the correct two rows on both surfaces; the owner's plan carries the multi-county / unresolved state. (Disposition per STANDING RULE #2: the fix removes the dependency on that input rather than relying on a repro.)
Shipped — **the location rule no longer reads any county the host identified.** Each source declares the real boundary it serves; both hosts and the map's draw filter ask the SAME pure function (`layerPanelModel.layerAvailableHere` → `inRegion` → `serviceAreas.areaContains`) with the SAME inputs (plan origin / finder view centre + state): `hcfcd_row` → **`harris`** (Harris County, from the same bundled county polygons `countyForView` uses — one definition of "Harris"); `coh_storm`, `coh_ww`, `coh_water`, `coh_hydrants` → **`houston`** = the **City of Houston limits ∪ its ETJ** (TxGIO City_Boundaries full-purpose + H-GAC `HGAC_City_ETJ_Boundaries` CITY='HOUSTON'; the real boundary WAS available, so the "Harris County" fallback was not used); `bkdd_drainage`, `bkdd_easements`, `bkdd_dmp` → **`bkdd`** (the Brookshire–Katy Drainage District boundary, Waller County GIS layer 54). The growth-fault row keeps a circle, renamed `houston_metro` — it is a metro-scale USGS study extent, which is what a circle is honest about. Data: `lib/serviceAreaData.js`, GENERATED by `scripts/build-service-areas.mjs` (committed; re-run to refresh), loaded by dynamic import (own chunk, nothing on the boot path) via `lib/serviceAreas.js` + `lib/useServiceAreas.js`. **Fails open** on: no location, geometry not loaded yet / failed to load (loud `console.error`), unknown area name (a unit test fails the build on a typo). The simplified boundaries are approximate (≈0.4 km), so a point counts as inside when ANY of five probes (the point and four ≈0.3 mi offsets) is — an approximation can only err toward SHOWING a layer. A layer left ON where its source does not serve is kept in saved state and simply not drawn (unchanged rule).
**Consequences owners should know:** downtown Houston no longer lists the three BKDD rows (it is outside that district — it used to list them because Harris is one of BKDD's counties); a Harris site outside Houston's limits+ETJ (Baytown's Harris side) lists HCFCD Channels & ROW but not the City of Houston Storm Sewer / Water & Sewer / Fire-hydrant sources; a Fort Bend site lists none of the Houston-area rows (Sugar Land used to list the BKDD ones).

- **CONFIRMED IN CODE FIRST, per the owner's own caveat.** The one bottom-center toast pill every `flashWarn(...)` call renders through (`SitePlanner.jsx`, near `toastPill`) picks its background from the message TEXT: `overlapWarn.startsWith("⚠") ? A call site that refuses a requested action but doesn't happen to prepend `⚠` therefore renders in the SAME green as a genuine success toast, or as the "● Scaled · county GIS" affirmative status chip the owner compared it to (a different component, `rgba(22,101,52,0.92)` — visually the same family of green, confirming the READING even though it's a separate element). This is exactly the shape B742368's own old refusal was in before this item's fix.
- **A SECOND, independent bug in the color rule itself, found while confirming the first.** `.startsWith("⚠")` misses any message that EMBEDS a warning mid-string rather than leading with it — e.g. `"All 3 deeds placed.${bad.length ? " ⚠ Verify: …" : ""}"` — which never starts with `⚠` even when it does carry one, so it also rendered green. Changed to `.includes("⚠")`, which catches both without touching any call site's wording.
- **THE AUDIT — every one of the 130+ `flashWarn(...)` call sites in `SitePlanner.jsx` was read and classified as a genuine blocking refusal/failure (needs `⚠`), a completed action (correctly green, left alone), or a neutral in-flight mode prompt ("Click the far side of the ditch.", left alone — not this report's shape).** ~24 of the clearest, highest-traffic refusals now carry the `⚠` prefix: both `place.mode === "refuse"` (LOUD-FAILURE) sites, the reshape self-intersection revert (B742369), footprint dock-wall-corner guards, "Couldn't delete/copy/duplicate/re-render/reach the hydrant source/sample 3DEP/form a shape/build that easement" failures, "No parcel/county-parcel/building/bearings…" and "Select a pond/plotted deed boundary first" preconditions, "That's already gone", "That drawing is locked", "This tab is read-only", pond-sizing refusals including the one that already says "refusing" outright, and the lock-toggle failure messages. **What was deliberately left green:** every message reporting a COMPLETED action even with a caveat (e.g. "Aligned…", "Pasted…", "Rotated the deed… ⚠ the fit is loose" — the embedded `⚠` there now correctly reddens it via the `.includes` fix, without touching its wording), and neutral step-by-step mode instructions during an armed multi-click flow (those aren't refusals and aren't this report's shape).

- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- **THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: filled AREA layers draw UNDER the site elements; LINE/stroke layers draw OVER them.** A contour crossing a building is a hairline and reads fine; a floodplain fill over a building buries it. That one distinction answers the complaint with no control at all — he sees his contours through his buildings, and his buildings never vanish under a blue wash. Neither Google Maps nor Apple Maps lets a user reorder layers; both use a fixed semantic hierarchy and expose opacity, which is exactly what shipped.
- **The model, in one place: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/mapStack.js`.** Bottom → top: basemap/aerial → GIS AREA layers → references → parcel → setback band → site elements → references explicitly promoted above the plan (B1198) → GIS LINE layers → labels and chips → manipulation handles. Every renderer names a tier from this file; nothing anywhere picks a z-index of its own.
- **Roles are DECLARED, never inferred at render time.** Every one of the 36 registered GIS sources carries an explicit `role: "area" | "line" | "point"` (points ride the over-the-plan band with the lines — burying a well or a hydrant under a pad defeats the point of turning it on). A source that publishes BOTH splits into its two roles via `roleLayers`: **FEMA** now paints its zone POLYGONS (sublayer 28) under the plan and its hazard BOUNDARIES (27) over it; **BKDD Drainage Information** splits sub-watersheds (116) from streams / BFE lines / outfalls (108, 121, 112, 2); **BKDD Master Plan** splits the study floodplains + proposed detention from the conveyance + proposed channel improvements. One panel row, one opacity, one status dot, two export requests.
- **The mechanism, and why it was not just a z-index.** Leaflet keeps every pane inside its own `_mapPane`, which carries the pan transform and therefore its own stacking context — so NO z-index on a pane can lift it above the planner SVG. The line-role pane is hosted OUTSIDE the map, in a sibling box above the SVG, with the two transforms that position it mirrored in the SAME statement as the original (VIEWPORT-STABLE): the wrap's live gesture transform and Leaflet's own map-pane translate. The host is `pointer-events: none`, so it can neither block a click nor steal a handle.
- **PDF-PARITY.** The sheet composites the same two bands: `under` at the backdrop anchor as before, `over` appended after the drawn plan and before the sheet furniture. Both raster and vector emitters take the band as an argument, so screen order and sheet order cannot drift.
- **NO new mode, NO keyboard shortcut, NO per-layer z-order UI** — asserted by a guard that fails if the Layers panel ever renders one.
